chapters.1: Joel describes a devastating locust plague that has stripped the land bare, destroying crops, wine, and food offerings at the temple. He calls priests and people to mourn and fast, treating the disaster as a warning sign of the coming "day of the Lord."
chapters.2: Joel pictures an invading army advancing like an unstoppable locust swarm and calls the nation to genuine repentance—turning to God with the heart, not just outward ritual. God responds by promising to restore the crops and reverse the devastation, and then promises to pour out his Spirit on all people, so that sons, daughters, young and old will prophesy and see visions.
chapters.3: God announces he will judge the nations that mistreated and scattered his people, gathering them for judgment in the "valley of decision." The book ends with a vision of restored blessing for Judah and Jerusalem, with the Lord dwelling among his people permanently.
